rules.opening_blocks_repeat.derivation: The opening ask is an offer made for every product (attempt 1), so a later step that repeats it counts as a repeat.

quotes: "It's too much" counts as a refusal of the step on the table.
rules.too_much_skips_full.derivation: 'Too much' refuses only the current step. Nothing says later full-amount steps are skipped.

rules.too_much_floor.requirement: "It's too much" counts as a refusal of the step on the table.
rules.too_much_floor.gap: Neither attempt_1 nor asked_date expresses 'too much' as a plain refusal of the current step with the ladder going on unchanged, without an early floor offer and without skipping later full-amount steps.

quotes: When the attempt limit of the band is reached, or the steps run out, the product ends without a promise and gets a refusal note.
accept it when the amount is at least the floor and the date is a business day no later than the deadline; otherwise explain the limit and go on with the next step.
rules.refuse_deadline_is_refusal.derivation: A proposal past the deadline is not accepted. The agent explains the limit and moves to the next step, so it counts as a refusal of the step.

assumptions: Order of authority: memo FL-OPS-26-11 overrides COL-POL-07 and CL-12, and the policy and code list override the email.

Calls are assumed to be on or after 30 Oct 2026, so memo items 1, 2 and 4 apply: band A deadline is the 5th business day after today, 2026-11-13 is removed as a closure day, 2026-11-30 is added, and the overdraft floor is 20%. Pre-memo behaviour is listed under unsupported_rules.
The email says 'three goes' for security, but policy 2.1 (two wrong answers in total end the check) wins, and the API agrees: max_wrong = 2.
The email says the loan floor is 'the monthly instalment, full stop', but policy 2.4 wins: the instalment in bands A and B, the full arrears in band C (floor_full_types).
Dispute note codes: NO-DSP and NC-DSP before 2026-11-18, NX-QRY from that date (event_changes). NL-DSP is unchanged.

Floors are computed as percentage, then round up to the step, then the minimum, then capped at the arrears. Example: card arrears £20 gives 3, rounded to 5, raised to 30, capped at 20. Card arrears £200 gives exactly 30, which stays 30. Overdraft arrears £310 gives 62, rounded up to 70.

The opening ask counts as attempt 1, so ladder[0] is 'full today'. Band A (3 attempts) and band C (3 attempts) never reach the floor step. In band C, the 'full on deadline' step equals 'full on 2nd business day', so it is skipped but still uses an attempt.
Band B deadline rolls to the last business day of the next month when today is that day or later (roll_if_not_after_today).

The brief says nothing about callbacks, third parties, wrong numbers, deceased customers or unclear confirmations. Default callback settings are used, and the outcome is not_reached with invented reason codes (callback, no_callback, wrong_number, deceased, unclear), because close_call requires a reason.
The service_error close reason is not given. 'system_error' with outcome no_promise is used. The note is N-SYS, per CL-12.
Hardship is transferred directly to the care queue with no notes. The hardship event is kept as handed_over/hardship for completeness.
Human transfer: the agent asks once whether it can help before transferring (default). The brief only says such callers go to General.
date_rules, confirm.max_asks, max_not_talk, after_promise and purpose_is_decline use the defaults because the brief is silent.
Postcode length varies, so no fixed length is set. The format is capital letters with one space before the last three characters. The birth year is four digits.
promise_change: the brief is silent, so the agent says the promise cannot be changed on this call.
No requirement to say the call is recorded, and no SMS line is given, so sms_line is empty.
